HF.all_components_mapped: All components from the HuggingFace model have been successfully mapped to their vLLM counterparts. The mapping includes the complete model hierarchy from root through all layers, including the ModuleList container (root.model.layers), attention mechanisms, MoE blocks, and normalization layers. The HF implementation embeds the TopK routing logic within the FusedMoE forward method via FusedMoE.select_experts(), so there is no separate TopK module in the HF architecture. The experts in HF are stored as fused weight tensors (w13_weight, w2_weight) within the FusedMoE class, not as individual module instances.

vLLM.root.model.layers.{i}.mlp.topk: This TopK component in vLLM does not have a direct structural counterpart in the HuggingFace implementation. This represents an architectural difference rather than a missing mapping. In HF, the expert selection and routing logic (TopK operation) is embedded within the FusedMoE.forward() method - when router_logits are passed to self.experts(), the FusedMoE internally performs TopK selection via the static method FusedMoE.select_experts(), which handles weight renormalization and routing. In vLLM (sglang fork), this logic is explicitly factored out into a separate TopK module (self.topk) that is called before the experts: topk_output = self.topk(hidden_states, router_logits), then final_hidden_states = self.experts(hidden_states, topk_output). The vLLM TopK module provides enhanced functionality including multiple output formats (TRITON_KERNEL, BYPASSED, STANDARD), grouped TopK support, custom routing functions, flexible renormalization strategies, correction bias support, and device-specific optimizations. While the functionality is semantically equivalent, this structural difference may introduce numerical differences in expert selection, weight normalization, and routing that could contribute to the accuracy drop observed in the bug report (Qwen2-57B-A14B-Instruct: 0.58 vs 0.86 accuracy). The TopK module should be examined for potential numerical precision issues, particularly in the routing, renormalization, and weight scaling operations.
